Bank of Queensland Reports Better-Than-Expected Annual Earnings
By Stuart Condie
SYDNEY--Australia's Bank of Queensland aims to start growing its mortgage book again after improved lending margins helped to support the regional lender's better-than-expected annual earnings.
BOQ on Thursday reported a net profit for the 12 months through August of 250 million Australian dollars, equivalent to US$174.3 million.

Cash earnings, a measure of profitability closely watched by analysts fell by 7% to A$358 million. However, the decline was smaller than the 13% fall expected by analysts, according to consensus data compiled by Visible Alpha.
The board held the final dividend at A$0.20 a share.
Net interest margin rose 60 basis points to 1.70% as Bank of Queensland focused on growing its business bank, while allowing less profitable home loans to roll off its book.
Commercial lending rose by 16% over the year, while mortgage lending fell by 8% as rising interest rates and slowing activity stoked increased competition among banks.
BOQ said it aims to maintain the pace of commercial lending growth in fiscal 2027, while also planning for what it called a sustainable return to growth in home lending.
"This will be enabled by expanding the group's digital mortgage to additional channels and customer segments," it said.
